title: Delegate vs closure vs NotificationCenter vs KVO vs Combine
summary: Objects talk to each other in a few standard ways. Pick by how many listeners there are and how tightly the objects are related.
body: **Delegate (one-to-one, many events):** a protocol the owner implements, held `weak`. Example: `UITableViewDelegate`. Clear contract, good when there are several related callbacks.
**Closure / callback (one-to-one, one event):** pass a function to call later, e.g. `onSave: (Item) -> Void`. Lightweight; watch for retain cycles.
**async/await (one request, one answer):** replaces many completion closures; easier error handling.
**NotificationCenter (one-to-many, loosely coupled):** broadcast by name; anyone can listen. Good for system events (keyboard shown, app backgrounded). Overuse makes flows hard to trace.
**KVO (observe a property):** watch an `@objc dynamic` property of an NSObject, often of Apple APIs (e.g. `AVPlayer.status`).
**Combine / AsyncSequence / Observation (streams of values):** for values that change over time with transformations (debounce, combine).
**Real-life analogy:** Delegate = your personal assistant. Closure = a sticky note "call me when done". NotificationCenter = a PA announcement in an office. KVO = watching a specific thermometer.
keyPoints: One-to-one: delegate (multiple callbacks) or closure (single callback); async/await for request-response.
Notifications are loosely coupled but hard to trace and untyped; prefer typed APIs inside your own code.
Choose the simplest mechanism that fits the number of listeners.

followups: **Delegate vs closure - when do you choose which?** Delegate for a group of related callbacks and data source style APIs; closure for a single simple callback.
**Why must a delegate be weak?** The delegate usually owns the object that holds it; strong both ways = retain cycle.
